original_question: Do stable GKK tau-matrices satisfy Newton's inequalities c_j^2 >= c_{j-1} c_{j+1} for the normalized sums c_j of principal minors described in the paper's Newton-inequalities problem?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 5b, the stable-subclass version of Problem 5 on Newton’s inequalities: whether stable GKK τ-matrices satisfy the inequalities c_j^2 >= c_{j-1} c_{j+1} for the normalized principal-minor sums c_j. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the Newton-inequalities part of the paper, the stable GKK τ-matrix subclass singled out as subproblem 5b, the quantities c_j as normalized sums of principal minors, and the intended inequality c_j^2 >= c_{j-1} c_{j+1}. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s official target is not the full Problem 5 but its explicit subproblem 5b, so the refined question should say that it is asking for the stable GKK τ-matrix case of the Newton-inequalities problem. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))

The ambient setting should be made explicit: A is an arbitrary complex n x n matrix, with n any positive integer. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))

The principal-minor notation should be defined: for α ⊆ {1,...,n}, A[α] means det A(α,α), and the paper sets A[∅] := 1. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))

The normalized quantities must be written explicitly as c_j(A) = (1 / binom(n,j)) sum_{|α|=j} A[α] for j = 0,...,n. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))

The inequality range should be stated exactly: c_j(A)^2 >= c_{j-1}(A) c_{j+1}(A) for every j = 1,...,n-1. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))

To be stand-alone, the term GKK should be unpacked: A is a P-matrix and is weakly sign-symmetric, meaning A[α,β] A[β,α] >= 0 for all almost-principal minors, i.e. minors with dispersal 1. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))

To be stand-alone, the term τ-matrix should be unpacked using the paper’s notation l(A) = min(σ(A) ∩ R), with min ∅ = ∞, together with eigenvalue monotonicity l(A(α,α)) <= l(A(β,β)) < ∞ whenever ∅ != β ⊆ α, and the extra condition l(A) >= 0. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))

The paper’s word stable means positive stable: every eigenvalue of A has positive real part, equivalently σ(A) lies in the open right half-plane. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))

No extra polynomial-style restrictions such as homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or asymptotic qualifiers occur in this problem; the essential missing information is instead the exact matrix-class definitions and universal quantifiers. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))
refined_question: Let n be a positive integer and let A ∈ C^{n x n}. For each j = 0,...,n, define c_j(A) := (1 / binom(n,j)) sum_{α ⊆ {1,...,n}, |α| = j} A[α], where A[α] = det A(α,α) is the principal minor indexed by α and A[∅] := 1. Suppose A is a stable GKK τ-matrix; that is, A is a P-matrix, it is weakly sign-symmetric in the sense that A[α,β] A[β,α] >= 0 for every minor of dispersal 1, it is a τ-matrix with l(A) := min(σ(A) ∩ R) (and min ∅ := ∞) satisfying l(A(α,α)) <= l(A(β,β)) < ∞ whenever ∅ != β ⊆ α and l(A) >= 0, and it is positive stable, meaning σ(A) lies in the open right half-plane. Must A satisfy Newton’s inequalities c_j(A)^2 >= c_{j-1}(A) c_{j+1}(A) for every j = 1,...,n-1? ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Section 3, Problem 5b rather than a broader neighboring question. In Section 3 the paper first defines c_j from normalized sums of principal minors and asks in Problem 5 whether any GKK τ-matrix satisfies Newton’s inequalities; it then immediately lists subproblem 5b for the stable GKK τ-matrix subclass. Section 2 supplies the definitions needed to make that subproblem self-contained: principal minors A[α], GKK, τ-matrix, l(A), eigenvalue monotonicity, and the meaning of stable. The nearby context on the same page explains the motivation: the authors originally hoped Newton’s inequalities might help imply stability, but they note that unstable P-matrices satisfying Newton’s inequalities exist, so the Newton-inequalities question itself remains open. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))
